To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified physiological (e.g. photosynthetic rates and water use efficiency) and molecular (e.g. glutathione, cysteine and methionine) traits that are associated with drought tolerance in Aleppo pine.
drought tolerant Aleppo pine provenances exhibit higher photosynthetic rates and water use efficiency, and increased concentrations of photosynthetic pigmens and soluble sugars.
we identified physiological and molecular traits that can be used as distinctive markers to select Aleppo pine provenances for drought tolerance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of distinctive traits to predict drought tolerance and the development of drought tolerant seedling production strategies for reforestation in arid environments.
the identification of drought tolerance in Pinaceae species.
identifying physiological and molecular markers of tolerance to drought in Aleppo pine seed sources, in order to predict the response of previously uncharacterized seed sources to water stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the physiological and molecular responses of Aleppo pine seedlings from drought tolerant seed sources to water deficit are characterized by an increase of water-use efficiency, a reduction of stomatal limitation and an enhancement of the photosynthetic capacity, which is accompanied by the accumulation of glutathione and sulfur amino acids, as well as the up-regulation of proteins associated with stress tolerance.

drought-tolerant provenances are those with a higher capacity of photosynthetic rate maintenance, higher levels of photosynthetic pigmentation, higher levels of glutathion and methionine and a higher number of proteins related to stress response and amino acid synthesis.

P. halepensis seedlings from the most drought tolerant provenances are more efficient in photosynthetic carbon gain, and in the synthesis and accumulation of soluble carbohydrates and amino acids, which may be related to the synthesis of glutathione.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the physiological and molecular characterization of seedlings from different provenances allowed us to identify drought-tolerant and sensitive seed sources.

drought tolerance is related with a combination of different traits, such as photosynthesis rate and water use efficiency, which are related to carbon fixation, and the accumulation of photosynthetic pigmentation and sugars.

drought tolerant provenances of Aleppo pine present a higher ability to tolerate drought stress in terms of physiological and metabolic responses, and this could be related to the increased levels of glutamine, glutamic acid and sulfur amino acids, which are related to the synthesis of osmolytes, and to the increased levels and expression of proteins involved in the protection against oxidative damage.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the physiological and proteomic profiles of drought-tolerant Aleppo pine seed sources are characterized by higher photosynthetic rates and water use efficiency, and higher glutathione, cysteine and methionine concentrations.
the identification of drought tolerant genotypes in Pinus halepisnsis is possible by combining different physiological and molecular approaches.

drought tolerant seedlings have a better photosynthetic performance, a more efficient photosynthetic machinery, and higher concentrations of sugars, glutathione, and methionine and that these traits can be used to predict drought tolerance.
